findings.label: Ecchymoses
findings.evidence: Ecchymoses (arrows) of the lower limbs in our case of Glanzmann thrombasthenia

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the lower limbs showing multiple ecchymoses (arrows), captioned explicitly as being from the authors' case of Glanzmann thrombasthenia; in-text mentions multiple ecchymoses predominantly on the lower limbs in this patient. Real patient photograph showing a specific mucocutaneous bleeding manifestation of the target disease, so it is included. Age group taken from the article title/in-text (14-month-old infant).
panels.attribution_text: Chemlal et al. Glanzmann Thrombasthenia in a 14-Month-Old Infant: A Rare Platelet Function Disorder Presenting With Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.108835. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ecchymoses (arrows) of the lower limbs in our case of Glanzmann thrombasthenia
in_text_mentions: On admission, the patient was alert and stable, with slightly pale conjunctivae. Physical examination revealed active gingival bleeding at the upper central incisor, a bruise on the lower lip, and multiple ecchymoses predominantly on the lower limbs (Figure 1), along with older lesions on the trunk. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy was detected, and the remainder of the examination was unremarkable.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial non-contrast CT slice (left half of the two-slice figure) of the reported Glanzmann thrombasthenia patient, with a red arrow marking a right lower lobe subpleural wedge-shaped opacity captioned as infarction. The article title is disease-focused (pulmonary thromboembolism in Glanzmann Thrombasthenia) and the panel-specific caption gives the manifestation, but this thrombotic/embolic complication is not one of the GT bleeding manifestations in the configured vocabulary, so no finding_key can be assigned and attribution rests on the case-level GT diagnosis; confidence therefore moderate. B: Second axial non-contrast CT slice of the same Glanzmann thrombasthenia patient, red arrow again indicating the right lower lobe subpleural wedge-shaped infarction described in the caption. Same limitation as panel A: the manifestation is a thrombotic complication and is absent from the provided GT finding vocabulary, so it is listed under...
panels.attribution_text: Mohammad Alizade et al. Pulmonary thromboembolism in Glanzmann Thrombasthenia: a case report and systematic literature review.. Annals of hematology 2026. doi:10.1007/s00277-026-06732-8. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Non-contrast CT showing right lower lobe subpleural wedge-shaped opacity (red arrow) consistent with infarction
in_text_mentions: Chest CT without contrast revealed a right lower lobe wedge-shaped consolidation consistent with infarction (Fig. 1). CT pulmonary angiography confirmed segmental PE within the right lower lobe pulmonary artery and subsegmental PE in the left lower lobe pulmonary artery, with associated infarctions in both lobes (Fig. 2). Echocardiography showed normal biventricular function and an estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) of 30 mmHg. Bilateral lower extremity Doppler ultrasonography was performed and revealed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis.
